children: FRENCH STOCKS ARE UNDERPERFORMING BUT NOT CHEAP ENOUGH TO BUY, SAY GOLDMAN
France's 2027 election is getting closer, and does appear to be weighing on stock markets
Goldman have a note out Thursday with a few striking statistics, and their conclusion is the underperformance is more likely to continue to extend than revert.
has been Europe's weakest large-cap index both this year and the past two, underperforming the STOXX 600 by 7.8% in 2024, 5.2% in 2025 and 6.8% in 2026.

That's not just to do with France, it maybe as much about weakness in luxury stocks who generate most of their revenues from abroad, but on Goldman's sums, almost every French sector trades at a discount to its European counterpart.
This implies "that investors are applying a broader 'France discount' on top of company- and sector-specific fundamentals."
But this discount might not be enough.
French bonds are also underperforming, the spread between the 10 year OAT and German Bund (DE10FR10=RR) is around 80 basis points, but has scope to widen further.

Goldman say historically a 10-bp widening in that spread means around 3% downside for the CAC 40 and 4% for their basket of French domestic focused stocks, but this time round stocks have not weakened as much as bond spreads would imply, partly due to resilient banking stocks.

"The OAT-Bund spread is back near the widest levels of the past five years, while the valuation discount of French domestic equities, even excluding Financials, remains broadly in line with its historical average," say Goldman.
"The bottom line is that neither French international equities, nor French domestic, appear to offer a completely clean value opportunity today," they say.
They prefer buying German stocks rather than French, and if French assets weaken further they prefer buying bonds ahead of stocks.
